text:
matt: quick summary from the perf run on mixed clusters — trying to land a conservative policy for max tokens-per-batch per cardclass (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100). results attached below, need feedback on enforcement vs. heuristic.

ana: saw the numbers, thanks. can you paste the core chart? rough take: H100 still tolerates high tokens, T4 less so.

matt: pasted the core table from the profiler:
```
device  | model   | avg_latency(ms/token) | max_tokens_safe
A10     | 7B      | 6.2                   | 2300
T4      | 7B      | 12.5                  | 900
L4      | 7B      | 9.1                   | 1200
A100    | 70B     | 4.9                   | 3200
H100    | 70B     | 3.8                   | 4200
```

matt: this is measured w/ KV cache warm and prefix batching enabled. note: when we disabled prefix caching we saw ~15-20% drop in throughput for A10/A100 on long-context workloads.

jess: that table helps. two flags: 1) those "max_tokens_safe" are conservative — but we need to fold in kernel fallbacks (FP16->FP32 kernel flops regressions). 2) KV fragmentation: mixed-length sequences cause underutilized slots, so effective tokens/batch is lower.

kai: ran a sim of batch formation with more aggressive packing: average batch tokens increased by 18% but tail latency (95th) spiked on T4 with some kernel fallback logs. attaching the snippet:
```
[2026-01-19T15:12:03Z] kernel-selector: fallback -> ampere_fp32_kernel (reason=kv_fragmentation>0.35)
[2026-01-19T15:12:03Z] scheduler: batch formed tokens=4100 device=T4 slots=4
[2026-01-19T15:12:05Z] request X: p95=1200ms
```

ana: okay so T4 is sensitive to kv_fragmentation threshold (0.35). we should cap per-device max_tokens so scheduler never forms >900 tokens on T4 in steady state. but allow transient bursts via burst credits.

matt: proposal: hard ceiling config per cardclass + soft target used by continuous batching heuristic:
- A10: ceiling=2600, target=2000
- T4: ceiling=1100, target=900
- L4: ceiling=1400, target=1100
- A100: ceiling=3500, target=3000
- H100: ceiling=4800, target=4200

jess: looks reasonable. suggest we also track kernel-selection rate and kv_fragmentation metric per-slot and add a fallback policy: if kernel fallback rate > 2% over 5m, lower target by 10%.

kai: implemented a test harness to exercise fallback policy. config snippet:
```
continuous_batching:
  target_tokens_per_batch: ${target}
  max_tokens_per_batch: ${ceiling}
  burst_credit: 2s
  fallback_policy:
    window: 300s
    threshold_rate: 0.02
    reduce_pct: 0.10
```

matt: can you run this for 4h across an A10 pool and a T4 pool and dump p50/p95/p99 + kernel-fallback-rate + kv_fragmentation histogram?

kai: scheduling a run now, ETA 4h. launching with canary label batchcap-v2.

infra-bot: deploy queued: canary/batchcap-v2 -> pool:a10-canary (3 nodes), pool:t4-canary (3 nodes). CI checks passed.

ana: one more operational ask — Console should show per-route effective target and current ceiling, so SRE can throttle at ingress if we see cross-pool overload. otherwise customer-facing latency will jitter.

matt: agreed. I'll open a small console PR to display route-level target/ceiling + kernel-fallback heatmap.

jess: also note for releases: include a short migration plan. teams with long-context workloads (search, code-gen) should opt into batchcap-v2 canary first.

matt: thanks. kai — tag me with results. I'll own the rollout plan and the migration doc. :thumbsup:

kai: will do. posting results in this thread when complete.

matt: action items summarized: 1) run 4h canary (kai), 2) collect metrics p50/p95/p99 + kernel fallback & kv hist (kai), 3) console UX PR (matt), 4) fallback policy guard added to runtime (jess to review). target: small gradual rollout next week if stable.

jess: ack.

ana: ack.

kai: starting run now (1764445600).

matt: thanks — closing for now, will wait for the metrics.
